message.reasoning_content:
Analyze the task carefully.

Task: Repair literal hash-suffix corruption in MarkdownFile heading titles only. In the current source, the title of "# C#" becomes "C", and heading/section search by "C#" fails. Within lines already recognized as ATX, only a trailing run of hashes separated from the preceding title by a space or tab is a closing marker. Attached hashes are to remain as literal title text, including when followed by trailing whitespace or a separate closing run. Preserve the current trim and separated-closer behavior, empty titles, levels, source line numbers, fence exclusion, hierarchy boundaries, search semantics, and exact original content. Markdown remains a narrow raw-text helper.

Baseline pattern:
r"^(?P<marker>#{1,6})[ \t]+(?P<text>.*?)[ \t]*#*[ \t]*$"

Candidate pattern:
r"^(?P<marker>#{1,6})[ \t]+(?P<text>.*?)(?:(?<=[ \t])#+)?[ \t]*$"

Diff: only that line of the pattern and one comment line.

Now let me analyze the behavior of the new regex.

Regex: ^(?P<marker>#{1,6})[ \t]+(?P<text>.*?)(?:(?<=[ \t])#+)?[ \t]*$

Key parts:
- marker: 1–6 hashes.
- [ \t]+: one or more spaces/tabs (the opening separator).
- text: .*? non-greedy.
- (?:(?<=[ \t])#+)?: an optional closing run of hashes, each with a space or tab immediately before it (lookbehind).
- [ \t]*$: trailing whitespace.

Text group followed by .strip() inside _parse_headings.

Case analysis:

1. # C#: marker #, space, then text must match .*, and after that the optional closing run (?:(?<=[ \t])#+)?, then [ \t]*$.

For "# C#": after the marker and space, the remainder is "C#". text is non-greedy, so it tries to take the smallest amount. text="" with (?:(?<=[ \t])#+)? at the position immediately after "# " (i.e., before "C#"): the lookbehind checks the character before the current position, which is the space. So (?<=[ \t]) succeeds, and #+ would match, but... the next character is "C", not "#". So #+ fails. The optional group matches empty. Then [ \t]*$ must match at the "C#" position, but "C#" is not whitespace, so it fails. Backtrack: extend text.

text="C" then: position is before the last "#". Optional group: lookbehind checks the character before the current position, i.e., "C", which is not a space/tab, so the lookbehind fails. The group matches empty (optional). Then [ \t]*$ at the "#" position: "#" is not whitespace and not end-of-string, so it fails.

text="C#" then: position is end of line. Optional group: lookbehind checks "#" — not a space, fails, matches empty. [ \t]*$ matches at end-of-string. So text = "C#".

Result: "C#". Correct — the attached hash is literal.

2. # C# #: remainder after "# " is "C# #".
- text="": at position before "C# #". Lookbehind: space (opening separator). #+ needs "#", but next char is "C". Fails. Group empty. [ \t]*$ fails ("C# #" isn't all whitespace). Extend.
- text="C": position before "# #". Lookbehind: "C", not space. Group empty. [ \t]*$ fails.
- text="C#": position before " #". Lookbehind: "#", not space. Group empty. [ \t]*$ at the " #" position: [ \t]* matches the space, then $ requires end-of-line but there is still "#". Fails.
- text="C# ": position before "#". Lookbehind: space. Succeeds. #+ matches "#". Then [ \t]*$ matches end-of-line. So text = "C# ". After .strip() → "C#". Correct — the trailing closing run separated by a space is stripped.

3. # Title #: similarly, text = "Title " → strip → "Title". Correct.

4. # ##: remainder after "# " is "##".
- text="": position before "##". Lookbehind: space. #+ matches "##". [ \t]*$ matches end-of-line. So text = "" → strip → "". Empty heading. Correct as expected.

Wait, but is that the intended behavior for an empty heading? The baseline pattern for # ##: [ \t]*#*[ \t]*$ — text is non-greedy: text="" then [ \t]* matches empty, #* matches "##", [ \t]*$ matches. text="" → "". So the baseline also produced "". The candidate preserves it. Good.

5. Attached hash with trailing whitespace: # C#  (two trailing spaces). Remainder: "C#  ".
- text="": position before "C#  ". Lookbehind: space. #+ needs "#" but next is "C". Fails.
- text="C": position before "#  ". Lookbehind: "C" fails. Group empty. [ \t]*$ fails ("#  " isn't all whitespace... wait, "#" is not whitespace, so [ \t]* matches empty, and $ fails).
- text="C#": position before "  ". Lookbehind: "#", fails. Group empty. [ \t]* matches "  ", $ matches. So text = "C#" → strip → "C#". Correct — attached hash with trailing whitespace remains literal.

6. Attached hash followed by a separate closing run: e.g., # C## #? Hmm, "attached hash followed by trailing whitespace or a separate closing run." Let me think: # C# # was already case 2. What about # C## # (a title "C##" with a closing run)? Remainder: "C## #".
- text="": lookbehind space, #+ needs "#" but next is "C". Fails.
- text="C": position before "## #". Lookbehind "C" fails. [ \t]*$ fails.
- text="C#": position before "# #". Lookbehind "#", fails. [ \t]*$ fails.
- text="C##": position before " #". Lookbehind "#", fails. Group empty. [ \t]*$ fails (space then #).
- text="C## ": position before "#". Lookbehind space, succeeds. #+ matches "#". [ \t]*$ matches. text="C## " → strip → "C##". Correct.

What about # C###? (attached hashes only, no closing run). Remainder "C###":
- text extends up to "C###": position at end, lookbehind "#" fails, group empty, $ matches. text="C###". Literal. Correct.

7. Tricky case: title ending in a space, then hashes — e.g., # Title # with a tab separator: # Title\t#. Remainder: "Title\t#".
- text="Title": position before "\t#". Lookbehind: "e", fails. Group empty. [ \t]* matches "\t", then $ fails (there is "#").
- text="Title\t": position before "#". Lookbehind: tab, succeeds. #+ matches "#". $ matches. text="Title\t" → strip → "Title". Correct — tab-separated closing run is stripped.

8. What about a heading with no title but hashes, i.e., # ##? (already covered, → "").

9. # # (a single hash after the marker): remainder "#".
- text="": lookbehind space, #+ matches "#", $ matches. text="". → "".
Baseline: text="" [ \t]* empty, #* matches "#", → "". Same.

10. What about #  # (two spaces after the marker, then #)? marker #, [ \t]+ is greedy, so it takes both spaces? Actually [ \t]+ is greedy: takes "  " (both spaces), position before "#". Then text="": lookbehind is space, #+ matches "#", $. text="". Same result.

But wait — a subtle point: greedy [ \t]+ vs. text. Consider # a  b # (two spaces between a and b, trailing closing). No problem.

11. Critical edge: # C# # where the attached hash run is adjacent to the closing run: # C#### #? Title "C####", closing "#". Remainder "C#### #":
- text extends: "C" (lookbehind "C" fails... wait, position after "C" is before "### #"; lookbehind checks the last consumed character "C", not a space, fails).
- ... text="C####": position before " #", lookbehind "#", fails. [ \t]*$ fails.
- text="C#### ": position before "#", lookbehind space, succeeds. #+ matches "#", $. text → "C####". Correct.
